claims.claim: Japan's tighter permanent-residency rules take effect in phases from October 1 and require household income above the Japanese average, applied retroactively to applications since April, plus Japanese-language proficiency and a pension pot equivalent to 30 years of payouts.
claims.episode_span: Applicants must show annual household income above the Japanese average
claims.source_title: Japan moves to tighten rules for foreigners, throwing futures into doubt
claims.supporting_quote: Under rules set to come into effect in phases from October 1, applicants for permanent residency will need to show that their annual household income exceeds the Japanese average – a stipulation that will be applied retroactively for applications submitted since April – and demonstrate Japanese-language proficiency.

claims.claim: Japan's Immigration Services Agency said foreigners need to live independently and have a stable life without the risk of becoming a burden.
claims.episode_span: foreigners need to “live independently” and have “a stable life without the risk of becoming a burden.”
claims.source_title: Japan moves to tighten rules for foreigners, throwing futures into doubt
claims.supporting_quote: In an announcement detailing the changes, Japan’s Immigration Services Agency stressed the need for foreigners to “live independently” and have “a stable life without the risk of becoming a burden”.

claims.claim: Abdul, a Bangladeshi tech engineer in northern Tokyo for nearly eight years, is preparing residency and citizenship applications and looking for work outside Japan.
claims.episode_span: Abdul, a Bangladeshi tech engineer who has lived in northern Tokyo for nearly eight years
claims.source_title: Japan moves to tighten rules for foreigners, throwing futures into doubt
claims.supporting_quote: “Right now, I am starting to look for opportunities outside of Japan.”

claims.claim: Sarah Nelkin, an American resident of 14 years, filed for permanent residency shortly before the announcement and says rejection would push her toward citizenship, which would require giving up US citizenship because Japan does not recognise dual nationality.
claims.episode_span: if she is rejected she will seek citizenship, which would mean giving up her United States citizenship
claims.source_title: Japan moves to tighten rules for foreigners, throwing futures into doubt
claims.supporting_quote: If her application is rejected, she plans to apply to become a Japanese citizen – which would mean giving up her US citizenship, as Japan does not recognise dual nationality.

claims.claim: President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday that Ukraine disclosed the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea in breach of a non-disclosure agreement, after President Zelenskyy told the UN General Assembly the soldiers had been sent.
claims.episode_span: Ukraine disclosed the transfer in breach of a non-disclosure agreement
claims.source_title: (2nd LD) Lee says Ukraine disclosed transfer of 2 N.K. soldiers in breach of non-disclosure agreement
claims.supporting_quote: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday expressed regret that Ukraine has disclosed the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to South Korea, calling it a breach of a non-disclosure agreement that he said may lead to many problems.

claims.claim: The Ukrainian presidential office said it disclosed only the transfer, not the long details, that keeping the entire transfer secret would have been strange, and that the transfer was done through direct dialogue with Seoul.
claims.episode_span: the country disclosed only the transfer, not what it called the long details of the process
claims.source_title: (2nd LD) Lee says Ukraine disclosed transfer of 2 N.K. soldiers in breach of non-disclosure agreement
claims.supporting_quote: Responding to a query from Yonhap News Agency, the Ukrainian presidential office said Thursday that the country has only disclosed the transfer of the North Koreans to South Korea without what it called the long details of the process, claiming that it would have been strange to keep the entire transfer a secret.
